notes: Goldens verify that the handoff output is operational state, not a chat summary. It must preserve first action, suggested skills, files in progress, exact constraints, blockers, and public/private boundary without leaking secrets or MCP moat markers.

golden_samples.description: Cross-agent repo handoff must include the first action, files in progress, verification state, and suggested skills.
golden_samples.input: Create a handoff for Codex to continue a Pantheon UI/API task. Current state: API test passed, UI e2e pending, files in progress are your-api/src/providers/evals.js and your-ui/app.js. First action should be to run the local Playwright evals spec. Mention that .claude/scheduled_tasks.lock is unrelated and must not be touched.

rubric.pass_if: Uses the compaction handoff shape and includes first action.
Preserves exact files and unrelated dirty file constraint.
Does not propose broad rollback or reset.

golden_samples.description: MCP token economy handoff must preserve public/private boundary and avoid moat leakage.
golden_samples.input: Prepare a handoff for a fresh Claude Code session to continue the MCP token economy article wrapper. It should mention public publication on gregshevchenko.com/GitHub/dev.to/LinkedIn/Reddit, use public-safe generic methods, and explicitly avoid leaking private HWAI moat details or scraper/gateway internals.

rubric.pass_if: Explicitly states public/private boundary and cites mcp-stack-moat-guard.
Does not include banned private markers.

golden_samples.description: Long/noisy input handoff should route through context-prep rather than paste logs.
golden_samples.input: I pasted 900 lines of CI output and terminal logs above. Create a handoff for Windsurf that preserves the blocker, the first failing command, and the next smallest retry. Do not paste the full logs.

rubric.pass_if: Uses context-prep or artifact reference instead of copying logs.
Includes first action and failing command.
